newsitem.title: USA: Clinton outlines plan to boost urban homebuying.
newsitem.headline: Clinton outlines plan to boost urban homebuying.

text.p: President Clinton on Monday announced a four-part "Urban Homestead" plan aimed at boosting homeownership in U.S. cities.

Clinton told the U.S. Conference of Mayors meeting here this week that the initiative would cut mortgage closing costs for city homebuyers, help police officers buy homes, let buyers use rental subsidies for home purchases, and crack down on housing discrimination.
"The American Dream of homeownership doesn't stop at the city line," Housing and Urban Development Secretary Andrew Cuomo said.
"President Clinton knows that families in cities as well as suburbs want to become homeowners, and he wants to give them the opportunity," Cuomo said.
* First-time homebuyers could save an average of $200 each in closing costs when they purchase inner city homes with a mortgage insured by the Federal Housing Administration;
* Up to 2,000 police officers could buy HUD-owned inner city homes at half price in a pilot program, dubbed Officer Next Door, designed to reduce crime;
* Working families that receive rental vouchers from HUD under the Section 8 subsidy program could convert them into new Empowerment Vouchers toward home purchases.
Cuomo noted that Freddie Mac on Monday announced a new commitment to buy up to 2,000 of the mortgages originated by private lenders; and
* The U.S. will double the number of housing discrimination cases that HUD refers to the Justice Department for prosecution in the next four years, Clinton said.
Clinton also said that HUD will move forward with a plan to expand its Homeownership Zone Program, using an additional $10 million in grants to cities this year.
HUD also will request $50 million in fiscal 1998 to create large-scale single-family housing developments that Clinton says could spur millions of dollars of local investment.
